pairs.title: Orchard spray and beehives
pairs.version_a: Dana grows apples next to a farm that keeps honeybees. One Friday afternoon she sprays her trees with a pesticide, although the wind is strong and the label warns against spraying in wind. She knows the spray might drift, but she wants the job done before the weekend. The spray drifts over the fence onto her neighbor's hives, and by evening every bee is dead from the pesticide. Later, inspectors test the hives. They find that the hives were free of disease, so if Dana had not sprayed, the bees would have lived on normally.
pairs.version_b: Dana grows apples next to a farm that keeps honeybees. One Friday afternoon she sprays her trees with a pesticide, although the wind is strong and the label warns against spraying in wind. She knows the spray might drift, but she wants the job done before the weekend. The spray drifts over the fence onto her neighbor's hives, and by evening every bee is dead from the pesticide. Later, inspectors test the hives. They find that the hives had a hidden disease, so even if Dana had not sprayed, the bees would have died of it by Sunday.
pairs.intended_difference: In A the hives were healthy so the bees would have lived without Dana's spraying; in B a hidden disease would have killed the bees by Sunday anyway.
pairs.judgment_question: How much is Dana to blame for the death of her neighbor's bees?
pairs.comprehension_question: According to the inspectors, what would have happened to the bees if Dana had not sprayed?
pairs.option_a: They would have lived on normally
pairs.option_b: They would have died of a disease by Sunday
pairs.option_c: They would have been moved to another farm
pairs.prediction_rationale: Readers still see Dana's spraying as reckless and as what killed the bees, but learning the bees were doomed by Sunday anyway should lower blame for their death by around a point.
pairs.originality_note: A new case of pesticide drift with a hidden disease that would have caused the same loss, not a re-skin of the poisoned-canteen or firing-squad cases.

pairs.title: Farm side gate
pairs.version_a: On a small farm, the goats spend each day in a fenced yard with a side gate. The farm has a rule: the side gate must stay latched until evening, because the goats push through it whenever it is loose. Kai started working on the farm that week. Kai knew about this rule. At noon on Tuesday, Kai unlatched the side gate to wheel a cart of hay through, and then left it unlatched. A few minutes later, Rosa, another worker, rattled a bucket of feed just outside the gate, as her job requires every day at noon. The goats rushed toward the sound, pushed the gate open, and ate the vegetables in a neighbor's garden. If the gate had been latched, or if Rosa had not rattled the bucket, the goats would have stayed in the yard.
pairs.version_b: On a small farm, the goats spend each day in a fenced yard with a side gate. The farm has a rule: the side gate must stay latched until evening, because the goats push through it whenever it is loose. Kai started working on the farm that week. Kai did not know about this rule. At noon on Tuesday, Kai unlatched the side gate to wheel a cart of hay through, and then left it unlatched. A few minutes later, Rosa, another worker, rattled a bucket of feed just outside the gate, as her job requires every day at noon. The goats rushed toward the sound, pushed the gate open, and ate the vegetables in a neighbor's garden. If the gate had been latched, or if Rosa had not rattled the bucket, the goats would have stayed in the yard.
pairs.intended_difference: In A Kai knew the rule that the side gate must stay latched; in B Kai did not know about the rule.
pairs.judgment_question: To what extent did Kai cause the goats to get into the neighbor's garden?
pairs.comprehension_question: Did Kai know about the farm's rule that the side gate must stay latched until evening?
pairs.option_a: Yes, Kai knew about the rule
pairs.option_b: No, Kai did not know about the rule
pairs.prediction_rationale: People single out a knowing rule-breaker as the cause more than an unknowing one when a routine co-contributor is also needed, but causal wording dampens the shift, so I expect roughly half a point to a point.
pairs.originality_note: A new farm setting with a physical gate-and-feeding mechanism and a knowledge manipulation, not the pen, computer-login or motion-detector vignettes.

pairs.title: Smoke alarm battery
pairs.version_a: Owen shares a flat with his friend Priya. Late one night, the hallway smoke alarm starts chirping every minute because its battery is low. There is no spare battery, the shops are shut, and Priya is asleep. To stop the noise, Owen takes the battery out, planning to buy a new one in the morning. He knows the alarm will not work until then. Later that night, a hidden fault in the building's wiring starts a fire. Because the alarm is silent, Priya wakes only when the flat is full of smoke, and she spends a week in hospital.
pairs.version_b: Owen shares a flat with his friend Priya. Late one night, the hallway smoke alarm starts chirping every minute because its battery is low. There is no spare battery, the shops are shut, and Priya is asleep. To stop the noise, Owen takes the battery out, planning to buy a new one in the morning. He knows the alarm will not work until then. Later that night, nothing goes wrong in the building. There is no fire, and Priya sleeps soundly until morning. Owen then buys a new battery and puts it in the alarm.
pairs.intended_difference: In A a hidden wiring fault starts a fire that night and Priya is hospitalized; in B nothing goes wrong and no one is harmed.
pairs.judgment_question: How wrong was Owen's choice to take the battery out of the smoke alarm?
pairs.comprehension_question: According to the story, what happened later that night?
pairs.option_a: Nothing went wrong and there was no fire
pairs.option_b: A hidden wiring fault started a fire
pairs.option_c: A burglar broke into the flat
pairs.prediction_rationale: Wrongness judgments are less outcome-driven than blame, but a serious injury to a flatmate should still make the same understandable choice look noticeably more wrong, by roughly one point.
pairs.originality_note: An everyday smoke-alarm battery choice in a shared flat, not Nagel's drunk drivers or published negligent-driving or poisoning moral-luck vignettes.
